newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A wave of London-based dollar demand swept the rand to a fresh two-month low on Thursday before it was shored up by exporter and offshore selling which carried it back to its overnight levels.

It was last quoted at 4.5515/5565, barely changed from Wednesday's 4.5510/5560 finish after touching a day's worst level of 4.5645 bid -- the weakest the currency has been since August 22 when it touched 4.5680 bid.
Dealers said the currency was initially hit by a large order out of London which caught the market short of dollars.
"We saw some heavy demand out of London by guys looking to take a punt at it," a dealer said.
The demand was pinned on rumours that IMF managing director Michel Camdessus' visit to South Africa was linked to an imminent announcement on the removal of exchange controls.
Camdessus will hold a press conference with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel at 1530 GMT on Friday.
Asked if there was any substance to the rumours, South African Finance Ministry spokeswoman Jennifer Wilson said: "No".
The initial flurry of demand drove the currency to it's weakest level by about 0700 GMT, where it hovered before retracing to its closing level.
"The guys who were buying dollars came in and took profits at just above 4.56," the dealer said, adding that exporter interest at the higher levels had aided the rand's recovery on the day.
The Reserve Bank was also rumoured to have assisted the market by offering dollars at the weaker levels, although this could not be confirmed.
Dealers said that in the medium-term, the rand was likely to hold in a 4.52 to 4.57 range, the latter expected to prove a difficult level to breach.
"We have had a double top at the 4.57 level so it should be quite a big resistance level," a dealer said in reference to chart factors.

Against the crosses, the rand regained some of its composure against the British pound to last trade at 7.2056/2168 from 7.2113/2215 previously, while against the mark, it was pegged at 0.3391/3396 from 0.3376/3381 overnight.
On the bond market, yields see-sawed in trade dictated largely by the rand's movements.
At the finish, the key R150 stock was pegged at 15.315 percent from 15.28 percent on Wednesday.
"We saw a bit of offshore selling, but it was mostly just tracking the rand," a dealer said, adding that volumes had been heavy during the morning session.
Dealers also noted that there was some concern about the continuing rise in short-term interest rates.
"People are still looking for money market rates to come off before we start moving lower again," one dealer added.
Three month NCDs quoted at between 16.10 percent bid and 15.95 percent offered from 16.05 to 15.90 overnight.

The 90-day BA rate was also quoted higher at between 15.55 and 15.35 percent from 15.45 to 15.35 percent range and the Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 7.612 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.641 billion rand on Tuesday.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 71.36 million rand worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling a net 31.81 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes rose to 4.22 billion rand on Wednesday from 3.68 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
